It is a common observation that the habits of a household take shape slowly and are changed more slowly still. What begins as a convenience becomes, in time, a custom; and what is once a custom is defended by all who have grown accustomed to it. Thus the prudent observer does not propose to alter at a stroke the practices of a house, but studies first the temper of those who dwell in it, and introduces improvement only by degrees, as the season and the occasion allow.
